headline: FDA approves new therapies across five cancers in November, including non-small cell lung cancer
dek: AJMC's roundup lists November approvals for head and neck, bladder, breast, non-small cell lung cancer and gastrointestinal stromal tumours, including two based on the OrigAMI-4 and VOLGA trials.
body:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) cleared new therapies in November for head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC), breast cancer, non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and gastrointestinal stromal tumours (GIST), according to a roundup by AJMC.

On 5 November 2026, the agency granted accelerated approval to amivantamab and hyaluronidase-lpuj (Rybrevant Faspro; Johnson & Johnson) for adults with recurrent or metastatic HNSCC whose disease progressed on or after platinum-based chemotherapy and immunotherapy. AJMC reported that this is the combination's first approval beyond NSCLC. The decision was based on Cohort 1 of the phase 1b/2 OrigAMI-4 trial, which enrolled 102 eligible participants. The confirmed overall response rate was 42% (95% CI, 32%-52%), with complete responses in 15% of patients and partial responses in 27%. Of participants in the cohort, 56% maintained a response for more than six months. Continued approval may depend on the phase 3 OrigAMI-5 confirmatory trial.

On 13 November 2026, the FDA approved perioperative durvalumab (Imfinzi; AstraZeneca) with enfortumab vedotin-ejfv (Padcev; Astellas/Pfizer) for adults with MIBC who are ineligible for, or have refused, cisplatin-based chemotherapy. In the phase 3 VOLGA trial of 695 patients, estimated 24-month event-free survival was 63.5% with durvalumab plus enfortumab vedotin versus 45.1% with surgery alone (HR, 0.51; 95% CI, 0.38-0.67). Estimated 24-month overall survival was 78.4% versus 69.4% (HR, 0.58; 95% CI, 0.40-0.83).
key_quote: the first and only dual-targeted therapy approved for this patient population

source.title: November FDA Approvals Bring New Options Across 5 Cancers

extra.scout_summary: A roundup of FDA oncology approvals in November 2026 across five cancer types, including a decision based on the ongoing phase 1/2 ALKOVE-1 study sponsored by Nuvalent.
